name: Medpor nasal implant

card.summary: A porous polyethylene implant placed on the nasal bridge to build up the dorsum, used in nasal reconstruction and augmentation for a straighter or higher profile.
card.note: Surgical implant; a fracture has been reported in a case report.

quick.overview:
Medpor is a porous polyethylene material that surgeons carve into implants. In the nose it is used to raise a low or collapsed bridge, such as a saddle nose after earlier surgery.

It helps looks by adding height and structure to the nasal dorsum, giving a more projected profile. Case literature describes it as an accepted synthetic option for nasal reconstruction.
quick.how: It is placed by a plastic or facial surgeon in an operation. Surgeons generally prefer a patient's own cartilage or bone when available, and use implants such as this where autologous grafts are not.
quick.risks: A 2002 case report described a Medpor nasal implant that fractured two years after surgery, causing asymmetry and a mobile step on the bridge [1]. Surgery carries general operative risks; implants may need revision.

lead: Medpor is a porous polyethylene implant material used in reconstructive and aesthetic surgery. In nasal work it is described in the literature as the most accepted alloplastic (synthetic) material for restoring the nasal framework [1].

It is used to rebuild or raise the dorsum, for example in saddle nose deformity after rhinoplasty. A case report describes a 24-year-old patient whose Medpor implant restored the dorsum with a result he appreciated for two years [1].
Surgical references generally favour autologous cartilage and bone for dorsal augmentation because of lower rejection risk, with synthetic implants used when grafts are not available [2].

chain: Implant placed on the nasal dorsum
angle.text: The implant builds up the bridge, so the nose appears straighter and higher.

paras: Medpor is used to restore the nasal dorsum [1]. Surgeons generally favour autologous cartilage and bone, with a synthetic graft as fallback [2].

A case report documents fracture of a Medpor implant two years after placement, with asymmetry and a mobile implant, confirmed on CT and ultrasound; the authors also described a new imaging method for the material [1]. They still described complication rates as low [1].
The one study found is a single case report on an implant fracture [1].

timeline.event: First case report of a broken Medpor nasal implant published [1].
